subQuestions.questionText:
The picture below illustrates … (Refer to the picture of a clock in the question paper.)
A seasonal time.
B daylight saving time.
C spring saving time.
D going home time.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (1 mark)
Daylight saving time. The clock illustration shows the practice of advancing the clocks during the warmer months.

subQuestions.questionText:
The international date line …
A is located 180° from the UTC.
B lies on the 150° east line of latitude.
C runs through Greenwich, a town near London.
D runs from east to west.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A (1 mark)
The international date line is located 180° from the UTC (Universal Time Coordinated).

options.B: lies on the 150° east line of latitude.
options.C: runs through Greenwich, a town near London.

subQuestions.questionText:
A visa is required to …
A travel in one's own country.
B apply for an international driving licence.
C enter the Schengen countries.
D buy duty-free goods.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C (1 mark)
A visa is required to enter the Schengen countries (a group of European countries with a common visa policy).

options.B: apply for an international driving licence.

subQuestions.questionText:
A scheduled tour will include …
A departure times that are not guaranteed.
B departure times determined by the tourists.
C departure times before sunrise only.
D set times of departure.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D (1 mark)
A scheduled tour has fixed/set times of departure that are pre-determined.

options.A: departure times that are not guaranteed.
options.B: departure times determined by the tourists.

subQuestions.questionText:
A business tourist who needs high-speed transport from OR Tambo International Airport to Sandton, will use the …
A Blue Train.
B Gautrain.
C Rovos Rail.
D Shosholoza Meyl.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (1 mark)
The Gautrain is a high-speed rail service that connects OR Tambo International Airport to Sandton.

subQuestions.questionText:
The Wailing Wall and the Dome of the Rock are both located in …
A Mecca, Saudi Arabia.
B Jerusalem, Israel.
C Yucatan, Mexico.
D Agra, India.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (1 mark)
Both the Wailing Wall (Western Wall) and the Dome of the Rock are located in Jerusalem, Israel.

subQuestions.questionText:
The province where the Richtersveld Cultural and Botanical Landscape is located:
A Gauteng
B Free State
C Limpopo
D Northern Cape
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D (1 mark)
The Richtersveld Cultural and Botanical Landscape is located in the Northern Cape province.

subQuestions.questionText:
This picture is associated with the … World Heritage Site. (Refer to the picture of the Golden Rhino artefact in the question paper.)
A iSimangaliso Wetland Park
B ǂKhomani Cultural Landscape
C Mapungubwe Cultural Landscape
D Maloti-Drakensberg Park
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C (1 mark)
The Golden Rhino is a famous artefact associated with the Mapungubwe Cultural Landscape World Heritage Site.

subQuestions.questionText:
The correct order in which the levies for marketing is collected:
A SATourism, TOMSA, Tourist, TBCSA
B Tourist, TBCSA, SATourism, TOMSA
C TOMSA, TBCSA, Tourist, SATourism
D Tourist, TOMSA, TBCSA, SATourism
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D (1 mark)
The correct order is: Tourist pays the levy, which is collected by TOMSA (Tourism Marketing South Africa), then channelled through TBCSA (Tourism Business Council of South Africa) to SATourism for marketing.

subQuestions.questionText:
A European platform used by SATourism to market South Africa internationally:
A Getaway Show
B ITB Berlin
C Africa's Travel Indaba
D Knysna Oyster Festival
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (1 mark)
ITB Berlin is a major European travel trade show in Germany used by SATourism to market South Africa internationally.

subQuestions.questionText:
The government department responsible for publishing and updating the Basic Conditions of Employment Act: (Refer to the department logos in the question paper.)
A Basic Education
B Home Affairs
C Labour
D Transport
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C (1 mark)
The Department of Labour is responsible for publishing and updating the Basic Conditions of Employment Act.

subQuestions.questionText:
Communication is an important … to have when delivering excellent service to customers.
A soft skill
B key word
C dress code
D hygiene practice
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A (1 mark)
Communication is an important soft skill in delivering excellent service.

subQuestions.questionText:
A hotel uses old bed sheets to create linen bags. This is an example of …
A restringing.
B restoration.
C repurposing.
D relaxation.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C (1 mark)
Repurposing means using something for a different purpose than originally intended (turning old bed sheets into linen bags).

subQuestions.questionText:
The amount offered by a tourist to a crafts person for the handmade item below: (Refer to the picture of a handmade vase in the question paper.)
A Bank rate
B Fair price
C GDP
D Income tax
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (1 mark)
Fair price is the amount that adequately compensates the crafts person for their handmade work.

subQuestions.questionText:
A code of conduct specifies how the staff members of a car rental company must …
A be paid their salaries.
B work together as a team.
C work a minimum number of hours.
D be contracted to perform core duties.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (1 mark)
A code of conduct specifies behavioural standards for how staff must work together as a team.

options.C: work a minimum number of hours.
options.D: be contracted to perform core duties.

subQuestions.questionText:
A form of payment that is no longer used when travelling internationally:
A Internet payments
B Credit cards
C Traveller's cheques
D Cash
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C (1 mark)
Traveller's cheques are no longer commonly used as a form of payment when travelling internationally.

subQuestions.questionText:
The multiplier effect is associated with …
A foreign exchange income.
B political instability.
C natural disasters.
D the outbreak of civil war.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A (1 mark)
The multiplier effect is associated with foreign exchange income, where money brought in by tourists circulates and benefits multiple sectors of the economy.

subQuestions.questionText:
An example of an unforeseen occurrence:
A Olympic Games
B Tsunami
C Wimbledon Tennis Championships
D COP27
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (1 mark)
A tsunami is an example of an unforeseen occurrence (a natural disaster that cannot be predicted in advance).

subQuestions.questionText:
In order for customers to give web-based feedback to a business, they will need …
A internet access.
B feedback cards and a pencil.
C a landline telephone.
D a hard copy of a survey form.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A (1 mark)
Web-based feedback requires internet access to submit responses online.

options.D: a hard copy of a survey form.

subQuestions.questionText:
An advantage for a country to host a global sporting event:
A Foreign exchange income
B Improve its political stance
C Exchange trade agreements
D Negative word-of-mouth
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A (1 mark)
Foreign exchange income is a major economic advantage for a country hosting a global sporting event.

subQuestions.questionText:
Give ONE word/term for the following description by choosing a word/term from the list below: remuneration; slogan; leave; branded product packaging; loss of culture; tourists' code of conduct; standard of living; green washing.

Hotel guests receive complimentary (free) toiletries containing the logo of the hotel in their rooms.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: branded product packaging (1 mark)
This refers to product packaging that displays the logo/branding of the hotel.

subQuestions.questionText:
Give ONE word/term for the following description by choosing a word/term from the list below: remuneration; slogan; leave; branded product packaging; loss of culture; tourists' code of conduct; standard of living; green washing.

The word/phrase associated with a tourism company.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: slogan (1 mark)
Accept also: branded product packaging.
A slogan is a memorable phrase used in marketing/advertising associated with a company.

subQuestions.questionText:
Give ONE word/term for the following description by choosing a word/term from the list below: remuneration; slogan; leave; branded product packaging; loss of culture; tourists' code of conduct; standard of living; green washing.

The period when staff is absent from work with permission from the tourism business.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: leave (1 mark)
Leave refers to authorised absence from work.

subQuestions.questionText:
Give ONE word/term for the following description by choosing a word/term from the list below: remuneration; slogan; leave; branded product packaging; loss of culture; tourists' code of conduct; standard of living; green washing.

Upliftment programmes have a positive impact on the local community by improving their …
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: standard of living (1 mark)
Upliftment programmes improve the overall quality of life and standard of living of communities.

subQuestions.questionText:
Give ONE word/term for the following description by choosing a word/term from the list below: remuneration; slogan; leave; branded product packaging; loss of culture; tourists' code of conduct; standard of living; green washing.

Only walk along clearly marked paths and walkways.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: tourists' code of conduct (1 mark)
This is a guideline of acceptable behaviour for tourists, including staying on marked paths.

subQuestions.questionText:
Choose the correct word(s) from those given in brackets.

Participating in programmes such as the (removal of alien plants/caging of wild birds) are excellent activities for environmentally conscious tourists.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: removal of alien plants (1 mark)
Removing alien (invasive) plant species is an environmentally beneficial activity. Caging wild birds is harmful to wildlife.

subQuestions.questionText:
Choose the correct word(s) from those given in brackets.

Staff of a travel agency visiting an orphanage to interact with the children is an example of (financial/non-financial) support.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: non-financial (1 mark)
Visiting and spending time is a non-financial form of support (no money involved, only time and presence).

subQuestions.questionText:
Choose the correct word(s) from those given in brackets.

To assist the guests at an accommodation establishment as best as possible is the (gratuity/conduct) expected from employees.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: conduct (1 mark)
Conduct refers to expected behaviour. Gratuity refers to a tip/payment.

subQuestions.questionText:
Choose the correct word(s) from those given in brackets.

Thinking on your feet to solve a customer's complaint requires (professional judgement/acting rudely).
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: professional judgement (1 mark)
Professional judgement is required to handle complaints effectively. Acting rudely is unprofessional.

subQuestions.questionText:
Choose the correct word(s) from those given in brackets.

Personal hygiene takes care of (body odour/mental health).
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: body odour (1 mark)
Personal hygiene relates to physical cleanliness and addressing body odour, not mental health.

subQuestions.questionText:
Choose a global event from COLUMN A that matches the description in COLUMN B.
COLUMN A: Tour de France
COLUMN B options: A world summit on climate change; B international tennis tournament; C international sports car race; D global cycling event; E multiple sports global event; F international golf tournament; G Netball World Cup
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: D (global cycling event) (1 mark)
The Tour de France is a famous global cycling event held annually in France.

subQuestions.questionText:
Choose a global event from COLUMN A that matches the description in COLUMN B.
COLUMN A: Formula 1
COLUMN B options: A world summit on climate change; B international tennis tournament; C international sports car race; D global cycling event; E multiple sports global event; F international golf tournament; G Netball World Cup
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: C (international sports car race) (1 mark)
Formula 1 is an international sports car (motor) racing championship.

subQuestions.questionText:
Choose a global event from COLUMN A that matches the description in COLUMN B.
COLUMN A: Wimbledon
COLUMN B options: A world summit on climate change; B international tennis tournament; C international sports car race; D global cycling event; E multiple sports global event; F international golf tournament; G Netball World Cup
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: B (international tennis tournament) (1 mark)
Wimbledon is one of the four Grand Slam international tennis tournaments held in London.

subQuestions.questionText:
Choose a global event from COLUMN A that matches the description in COLUMN B.
COLUMN A: Olympic Games
COLUMN B options: A world summit on climate change; B international tennis tournament; C international sports car race; D global cycling event; E multiple sports global event; F international golf tournament; G Netball World Cup
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: E (multiple sports global event) (1 mark)
The Olympic Games is a multi-sport global event featuring athletes from around the world competing in many sports.

subQuestions.questionText:
Choose a global event from COLUMN A that matches the description in COLUMN B.
COLUMN A: COP27
COLUMN B options: A world summit on climate change; B international tennis tournament; C international sports car race; D global cycling event; E multiple sports global event; F international golf tournament; G Netball World Cup
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: A (world summit on climate change) (1 mark)
COP27 (Conference of Parties 27) is a world summit on climate change held under the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change.

subQuestions.questionText: Complete the profile on Lythe Pillay according to the table below: (a) Nationality, (b) Age group, (c) Special interest. (Refer to the World Under-20 Championship information in the question paper.)

Mark allocation (1 mark each):
(a) Nationality: South African
(b) Age group: Under 20 / U/20 / Junior
(c) Special interest: Athletics / Running / Sprinting / Sports

subQuestions.questionText: The athletes required travel documents for the trip to the world championships. Name THREE documents they require when visiting Colombia.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 1 mark for each correct document (max 3 marks):
• A valid passport
• A valid visa
• A valid health certificate
• Proof of a Covid-19 vaccination / Covid-19 vaccination certificate

NOTE: Accept passport, visa and health certificate.

subQuestions.questionText: Give ONE travel condition the athletes likely suffered from when they arrived in Colombia.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer (2 marks): Jet lag

subQuestions.questionText: Give a definition of the travel condition identified in QUESTION 2.1.3.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer (2 marks): The physical condition that arises from crossing many time zones.

subQuestions.questionText: The effects of the travel condition identified in QUESTION 2.1.3 could have been reduced during the flight. Explain ONE way how the effects could have been reduced.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for ONE explained answer:
• Drink plenty of fluids especially water to prevent dehydration.
• Get lots of rest.
• Try to avoid caffeine and alcohol as it affects sleep patterns.
• Regularly stretch and walk around the cabin.
• Avoid taking sleeping medication on the flight.
• Eat light/healthy meals on board.
• Watches could be adjusted to the time at the destination. This will help the athletes to adjust to the new time zone.

subQuestions.label: 2.1.6(a)
subQuestions.questionText: The team was advised on health and safety precautions while visiting Colombia. Give ONE health precaution.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for ONE health precaution:
• Take the compulsory and required vaccinations.
• Drink bottled water only.
• Be cautious when buying street food.
• Wear sun block during the day.
• Have a sufficient supply of prescribed medication if required.
• Sanitise/wash your hands regularly.

subQuestions.label: 2.1.6(b)
subQuestions.questionText: The team was advised on health and safety precautions while visiting Colombia. Give ONE safety precaution.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for ONE safety precaution:
• Do not carry large sums of cash when out and about.
• Avoid a public display of expensive phones, cameras, jewellery and other valuables.
• Keep valuable personal items safely locked away.
• Never leave your luggage unattended.
• Carry wallets in an inside pocket and not in a back pocket.
• Do not walk alone in dark isolated areas.
• Move around and explore in groups.
• Avoid using ATMs/withdrawing cash at night.
• Exchange currency at a reputable FOREX retailer.

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate the time and date in Frankfurt, Germany when the team departed from South Africa. (Refer to the World Time Zone map and flight information in the question paper. Departure: Johannesburg 18:00 on 15 July 2022; Johannesburg is +2; Frankfurt is +1.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark allocation (4 marks):
Mark 1: Time difference = 1 hour
Mark 2: Calculation: 18:00 (-) 1 hour
Mark 3: Time in Frankfurt = 17:00
Mark 4: Date = 15 July 2022

Answer: 17:00 on 15 July 2022

subQuestions.questionText: The team was in transit in Frankfurt. Explain the term in transit.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer (2 marks): In transit means the team will have to wait at the airport before taking the flight to Colombia.

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate the time and date when the team arrived in Cali, Colombia. (Frankfurt arrival: 04:00; Time in transit: 2 hours; Departure from Frankfurt: 06:00; Flying time Frankfurt to Cali: 12 hours; Frankfurt is +1, Cali is -5.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark allocation (4 marks):
Mark 1: Time difference Frankfurt to Cali = 6 hours
Mark 2: Departure from Frankfurt = 06:00 (after 2 hours transit from 04:00)
Mark 3: Time in Cali at departure = 06:00 (-) 6 hours = 00:00; Plus flying time 12 hours = 12:00
Mark 4: Arrival date = 16 July 2022

Answer: 12:00 on 16 July 2022

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate the total duration (in hours) of the team's trip from Johannesburg to Cali.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark allocation (2 marks):
Calculation: 11 hours (flying time to Frankfurt) + 2 hours (transit) + 12 hours (flying time to Cali) = 25 hours

Answer: 25 hours

subQuestions.questionText: Explain the term duty-free.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer (2 marks): Duty-free means that goods and items within the allowed limits/amounts can be brought into the country without the need for a passenger to pay any additional taxes.

subQuestions.questionText: The team bought souvenirs from duty-free shops in Colombia (Colombian coffee, local handicrafts, gold/diamond jewellery valued at R30 000, and 1 litre of Aguardiente). Name the customs channel they had to pass through on arrival in South Africa.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer (2 marks): Red channel

subQuestions.questionText: Explain ONE reason for the team's choice in QUESTION 2.3.2.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer (2 marks): The value of the purchased jewellery (R30 000) exceeded the duty-free allowance in South Africa.

subQuestions.questionText: Name the government department responsible for Customs and Excise at airports.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer (2 marks): South African Revenue Services / SARS

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate, in rand, the total cost of Anne's trip to London. Trip lasted 5 days (4 nights). Costs: Return flight ticket R11 905; Train transport in London R185; Accommodation per night (room only) R1 060.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark allocation (3 marks):
Mark 1: Return flights = R11 905
Mark 2: Train transport = R185; Accommodation: R1 060 x 4 nights = R4 240
Mark 3: Total = R11 905 + R185 + R4 240 = R16 330

Answer: R16 330

NOTE: Do not penalise candidates if the currency code/symbol is omitted, as it is given in the question.

subQuestions.questionText: Give ONE other essential item (something Anne cannot live without) that had not been included in the budget above.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer (2 marks): Meals

NOTE: Accept examples of food/food items/types of meals.

subQuestions.questionText: Give the currency codes for the following: (a) Euro, (b) British Pound, (c) Australian Dollar.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark allocation (1 mark each):
(a) Euro: EUR
(b) British Pound: GBP
(c) Australian Dollar: AUD

subQuestions.questionText: Anne exchanged R30 000 at OR Tambo International Airport to cover her other expenses in London. Calculate the amount Anne received in the currency used in London. (BSR for British pound: 20.69; BBR: 19.50)
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark allocation (3 marks):
Mark 1: Use BSR (Bank Selling Rate) of 20.69 (bank is selling pounds to Anne)
Mark 2: Calculation: R30 000 ÷ 20.69
Mark 3: Answer: £1 449.98

Answer: £1 449.98

Note: Currency code or symbol to be indicated in the final answer.

subQuestions.questionText: When Anne returned home she had £177 left which she exchanged at a local South African bank. Calculate the amount she received in rand. (BBR for British pound: 19.50; BSR: 20.69)
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark allocation (3 marks):
Mark 1: Use BBR (Bank Buying Rate) of 19.50 (bank is buying pounds from Anne)
Mark 2: Calculation: £177 × 19.50
Mark 3: Answer: R3 451.50

Answer: R3 451.50

subQuestions.questionText: Name the country where the windmills in Kinderdijk are located.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer (2 marks): The Netherlands

subQuestions.questionText: Discuss TWO reasons why this attraction (Kinderdijk) is considered a world icon.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for each discussed reason (max 4 marks):
• UNESCO declared it a World Heritage Site to preserve and protect the windmills for future generations.
• It is a symbol of the struggle against water and flooding by the Dutch people.
• It is unique to the region and the Netherlands.
• It preserves the traditional technology used, for example milling grain.

subQuestions.label: 4.4.1(a)
subQuestions.questionText: Identify the review number that will encourage tourists with special needs to visit the attraction. (Refer to the reviews in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText: Answer (1 mark): Review 3

subQuestions.label: 4.4.1(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Give ONE example in the review to support your answer to QUESTION 4.4.1(a).
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for ONE example:
• All the tour boats have ramps for wheelchair users.
• Well-maintained and safe place.

subQuestions.questionText: State THREE other factors in the reviews that contribute to the success of the attraction.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 1 mark for each factor (max 3 marks):
• Effective behaviour of the staff and management
• Upkeep and maintenance of the site
• Positive experience of the visitors
• Safety and crime prevention

subQuestions.questionText: Give ONE reason why April to September in A are the best months to visit Kinderdijk. (Refer to the infographic in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for ONE reason:
• April to September is spring, summer and autumn months in the Northern hemisphere.
• Days are warmer and this will lead to a better visitor experience.
• The tulips are in full bloom and add to the scenery/beautiful landscape.

subQuestions.questionText: Refer to B. Suggest times that tourists should visit the windmills to avoid overcrowding.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks (1 mark each for two times):
• Before 12:00
• After 14:00

subQuestions.questionText: Identify ONE characteristic from C that indicates the success of the windmills as a tourist attraction.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for ONE characteristic:
• The high number of visitors (600 000) to the site
• Repeat visits

subQuestions.label: 4.5.4(a)
subQuestions.questionText: Explain the meaning of 1 : 10 000 #masstourism.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks:
• It means that for every one person living at Kinderdijk, the site receives 10 000 tourists per year.
• Refers to over-tourism/mass tourism.

subQuestions.label: 4.5.4(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Discuss ONE negative impact on the residents of Kinderdijk as a result of the concept explained in QUESTION 4.5.4 (a).
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for ONE discussed impact:
• No privacy for the permanent residents.
• Tourists damage their private property.
• Strain on the resources of the area.
• Higher levels of pollution – land, air, water, noise
• Degradation of the natural environment by people trampling on natural vegetation.
• Traffic/human congestion
• Loss/degradation of culture
• Elevated prices on items available at local businesses.

subQuestions.questionText: Refer to the map and identify the World Heritage Site that stretches along the border of South Africa and a neighbouring country. (Refer to the World Heritage Sites of South Africa map in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for any ONE of the following:
• F / Maloti-Drakensberg Park
• A / Mapungubwe Cultural Landscape
• B / Barberton Makhonjwa Mountains

subQuestions.questionText: Explain why the site identified in QUESTION 5.1 attracts different types of tourists.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for an explanation linked to the chosen site:

F (Maloti-Drakensberg Park):
• It is a mixed site that will comply with the international tourist's preferences.
• The site has both natural and cultural aspects for which it was declared.

A (Mapungubwe Cultural Landscape):
• It is a cultural site that shows the remains of an early civilisation and their trading.
• Artefacts like the Golden Rhino were found at the site.

B (Barberton Makhonjwa Mountains):
• It is a natural site that shows signs of early life in rock formations.
• The site includes the Geotrail that tourists can follow.

subQuestions.questionText: Apart from the province where the site in QUESTION 5.1 is located, suggest ONE other province where the tourist will find both natural and cultural World Heritage Sites.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for ONE province:
• Western Cape province
• Northern Cape province
• North West province
• KwaZulu-Natal province

subQuestions.questionText: Explain ONE reason why the natural site in the province identified in QUESTION 5.3.1 has World Heritage status.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for ONE reason linked to chosen province:

Western Cape: Cape Floral Region Protected Areas
• It is a hotspot for biodiversity of plant species.
• Home to the fynbos species that includes the national flower, the King Protea.
• It includes a famous landmark of the region - Table Mountain, one of the New Seven Natural Wonders of the World.

Northern Cape: Richtersveld Cultural and Botanical Landscape
• It is a rich diverse botanical landscape and reflects long-standing and persistent traditions of the Nama people.

North West: Vredefort Dome
• It is a meteorite impact site showing geological evidence of the impact.

KZN: iSimangaliso Wetland Park
• Five ecosystems operating in harmony.

subQuestions.questionText: Identify the city where the WTM Africa was held in April 2023. (Refer to the WTM 2023 picture in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText: Answer (2 marks): Cape Town

subQuestions.questionText: SATourism uses this event in South Africa as a marketing platform. The event prepares SATourism for future marketing initiatives in other countries. Do you agree with the statement above? (Yes/No) Give ONE reason for your answer.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for ONE reason. NOTE: Do not award marks for Yes/No.

YES:
• Initiatives at the WTM can be duplicated as initiatives at other events.
• Organisational problems can be limited and not repeated at future events.
• WTM Africa is a dry-run opportunity to prepare for the WTM and similar events hosted abroad.

OR

NO:
• Different event organisers have different requirements.
• Each event is unique in its focus.
• SATourism must target their marketing efforts to specific market segments according to the statistics of incoming tourists.

subQuestions.questionText: In a paragraph, discuss THREE reasons why this event is considered an excellent opportunity for tourism product owners to expand their target markets. Your discussion must include THREE of the four bullet points in the picture (180 speakers; 78 content sessions; 100 participating countries; 6 579 scheduled meetings).
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for each reason discussed (3 x 2 = 6 marks):

Speakers:
• 180 speakers will be sharing information.
• Many speakers will alert the attendees to many marketing opportunities available.
• Speakers will raise awareness of available products.

Content sessions:
• The content sessions will be about information sharing.
• Networking opportunities between the different stakeholders happen during content sessions.

Participating countries:
• 100 participating countries increase marketing opportunities.
• Increased market share amongst African countries.

Scheduled meetings:
• The scheduled meetings involve business networking opportunities.
• Closing of deals and bi-lateral agreements between businesses and/or organisations.

subQuestions.questionText: Give ONE reason why the people in the photo are all wearing the same uniform. (Refer to the airline cabin crew photo in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for ONE reason:
• They are cabin crew members of a specific airline.
• They have a set way of dressing.
• They portray the company image.
• They look more professional.
• They are part of a team.
• There is a standard to uphold.
• It is the starting point of standardising all levels of service.

subQuestions.questionText: Name the document set by the airline where the basic conditions of employment on duties and punctuality are given to the cabin crew.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks:
• Contract of Employment
• Employment agreement/contract

subQuestions.questionText: Name the category in the document identified in QUESTION 7.2.1 where discounted airline tickets for crew members are given.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks:
• Travel benefits
• Fringe benefits

subQuestions.questionText: Choose the correct phrase within brackets. Treating passengers professionally can be regarded as (termination of service/service ethics).
subQuestions.memoText: Answer (2 marks): service ethics

subQuestions.questionText: Explain ONE reason for your answer to QUESTION 7.3.1.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for ONE reason:
• All passengers have the right to be treated with respect.
• Equal and fair treatment of one's clients is essential.
• Professionalism is part of excellent customer service.

subQuestions.questionText: Discuss TWO reasons why it is a requirement for airline staff to pass job-related examinations every year.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for each reason discussed (max 4 marks):
• It is a requirement to ensure the safety of passengers.
• They must constantly up-skill their knowledge.
• They must stay up-to-date with the latest trends and standards of service.
• Both their theoretical and practical knowledge and skills are assessed.
• They must be medically fit for the long hours in the air, on their feet attending to passengers.
• They must be fit both physically and mentally.

subQuestions.questionText: A guest pays for a treatment at the wellness centre. Identify the pillar of sustainable tourism: Only natural ingredients are used for the treatments.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer (2 marks): environmental pillar / planet

subQuestions.questionText: Identify the pillar of sustainable tourism: The therapists offering the treatment are employed from the local community.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for any ONE:
• economic pillar / profit
• social pillar / people

subQuestions.questionText: As part of the Organic Green Spa's corporate social investment (CSI), they would like to give back to the community. Suggest ONE CSI initiative the spa can offer to the local community.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for ONE CSI initiative:
• The local community can receive complimentary treatments.
• Give discounted rates for individuals from the community.
• Family members of staff from the local community can be treated free of charge during not-so-busy times.
• Allow job shadowing by individual learners from a local secondary school in the spa with the permission from the guest being treated.
• Wellness awareness
• Upgrading local schools
• Assisting and developing the local community projects.

subQuestions.questionText: Suggest TWO ways how the water bottle policy at the lodge contributes to sustainable waste management.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for each way (max 4 marks):
• The single-use of plastic items are eliminated.
• There is a reduction of plastic going to the landfill.
• The reuse of water bottles by guests during their stay lessens the need for disposal.
• Bottles made of sustainable materials like glass are placed in hotel rooms and at the spa.

subQuestions.questionText: Using the information, give ONE example of procurement of local goods at the lodge.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for ONE example:
• The natural ingredients are harvested by the local community.
• The local communities supplying the lodge with products and services through their micro-enterprises.

subQuestions.questionText: Discuss ONE initiative by the lodge to reduce the impact of the current electricity crisis.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for ONE initiative discussed:
• The lodge invests in solar farms which use ample sunshine in South Africa to generate electricity.
• Through responsible tourism the lodge generates income which is spent on initiatives generating electricity benefiting many others.
• An alternative energy source through solar power can have excess electricity fed into the national grid.

subQuestions.questionText: According to Fair Trade Tourism (FTT), a certified tourism business like Rhino Ridge Lodge must practise the FTT principles. This must also be evident in their mission statement (written main goal or aim) and implemented by employees. Develop a mission statement (of not more than one sentence) for the Rhino Ridge Lodge that reflects 'Fair Say', one of the 6 FTT principles.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for a mission statement that reflects the FTT principle of Fair Say. To reflect:
• The local community leaders must be involved and consulted.
• BBBEE partners/stakeholders must be part of the decision-making process in conjunction with owners.
• All staff members and management to take collective decisions through meetings, staff surveys etc.
• The fairness of having stakeholder participation in decision-making.

Example mission statement: 'At Rhino Ridge Lodge, we are committed to involving all stakeholders, including local community leaders, staff, and BBBEE partners, in transparent and collective decision-making to ensure fair and equitable participation in our business.'

subQuestions.questionText: Give ONE reason why the World Table Tennis Championships is regarded as a global event. (Refer to the 2023 World Table Tennis Championships information in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for ONE reason:
• More than 400 players from 227 countries participated.
• Participants, representatives, spectators and media personnel came from all over the world.

subQuestions.questionText: Explain TWO reasons why Durban was an ideal venue for the championships.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for each explained reason (max 4 marks):
• Durban has the infrastructure, transportation networks, hotels, restaurants, lively entertainment spots and has among the world's best sporting venues.
• A unique African experience, perfect climate and the most welcoming people in the world.
• Durban has partnered with the SA Table Tennis Board, KZN Tourism and all their stakeholders to ensure that the world knows KZN is a magnificent and a must-see province.
• Durban has everything to ensure a unique visitor experience, such as beautiful scenery and landscapes, flora, fauna, and culture, heritage, Zulu experience, pristine beaches, perfect climate and the friendliest people.

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO positive impacts the championships had on the economy of Durban.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for each positive impact (max 4 marks):
• Tourists that attended the event contributed to foreign exchange earnings.
• The income generated by the event contributed to the GDP of the country.
• Infrastructure could have been improved.
• The event put the multiplier effect into motion which benefited the local economy.
• Job creation: workers earned money at the event.
• Income was generated before, during and after the Championships.
• Entrepreneurial opportunities were created for locals.
• Good publicity for Durban, locally and internationally.

subQuestions.questionText: Identify the type of unforeseen occurrence in the information. (Refer to the Hurricane Ian information in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for any ONE:
• Hurricane
• Natural disaster
• Hurricane Ian
• Flood
• Cyclone
• Tropical storm
• Typhoon

subQuestions.questionText: Name the TWO forces of nature that caused the most destruction to tourism infrastructure in Florida and South Carolina.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 1 mark each (max 2 marks):
• Flooding
• Strong winds
• Storms
• Heavy rainfall

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO ways how damage to the causeway may impact on tourism to the islands.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for each impact stated (max 4 marks). Accept perspectives from tourism and tourists:
• Tourism infrastructure such as hotels and restaurants on the islands had been destroyed and tourists will not be able to visit any of the islands.
• Tourists had to cancel their trips as they will not be able to access any of these islands.
• Tourism businesses on the islands will lose income due to the destruction, as no tourists will visit the islands.
• Workers at the hotels might have lost their jobs.
• Tourists visiting the islands before the hurricane struck, had to be rescued. They might have lost their belongings due to the hurricane and the collapse of the causeway.
• Tourists will not be able to continue with their itineraries due to the collapse and inaccessibility of the causeway.

subQuestions.questionText: Give the highest percentage of inbound international tourists to South Africa in the 2019/2020 period. (Refer to the graph on Main Purpose of Visit for International Tourist Arrivals in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText: Answer (2 marks): 41.4%

subQuestions.questionText: Apart from VFR, give the purpose of visit that received the highest percentage of visitors in 2020.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer (2 marks): Shopping

subQuestions.questionText: Give ONE reason why the purpose of visit identified in QUESTION 9.3.2 had such a high percentage of inbound visitors.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for ONE reason:
• Visitors from neighbouring countries crossed the border into South Africa to do shopping.
• Essential goods were unavailable in some of the neighbouring countries because of Covid-19. Individuals and businesses had to come to South Africa to do their business.
• Visitors from neighbouring countries are counted as tourists every time they cross the borders into South Africa, for whatever reason.
• Refund scheme for international visitors, allowing them to claim back the VAT paid.
• Currency advantage made shopping in South Africa more affordable for visitors from countries with stronger currencies.
• During Covid-19, visitors to South Africa were restricted to travel to other international destinations. South Africa was their closest destination.

subQuestions.questionText: Identify the method used to share customer satisfaction. (Refer to the customer feedback diagram in the question paper showing one person sharing a positive experience with many others.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for any ONE:
• Word of Mouth / WOM
• Verbal advertising
• Positive customer experiences
• Sharing positive customer experiences with friends/relatives

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO ways in which the method in QUESTION 10.1 will impact positively on the hotel.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for each way stated (max 4 marks):
• People tend to react positively to verbal advertising from people they trust.
• It is a fast and free form of direct advertising.
• Word-of-Mouth advertising is usually trustworthy.
• This type of advertising is aimed at a specific target market such as friends, family or co-workers.
• The verbal information is opinion-based on a positive experience and will influence more customers to stay at the hotel.
• An increase in income and profit for the hotel.
